title: Geometry-aware Test-Time Adaptation on Graphs

problem.claim: Test-time adaptation on graphs must handle distribution shifts in graph-structured data whose semantic similarity and topology-induced variations exhibit different geometric patterns.

gap.claim: Existing graph test-time adaptation methods use graph augmentations and self-supervised objectives in Euclidean space, while relying on a single fixed geometry can distort representations and mislead test-time updates.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes GeoTTA, a geometry-aware test-time graph adaptation framework that explicitly controls test-time update directions.
GeoTTA decomposes graph representations into hyperspherical and hyperbolic subspaces to capture semantic and structural variations in target samples, respectively.
The framework uses a joint geometry-aware adaptation objective for prototype alignment and geometric consistency on curvature-matched manifolds.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe GeoTTA as a novel geometry-aware test-time graph adaptation framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on ten public benchmarks reportedly demonstrate superior source-free test-time adaptation performance across diverse domains with competitive efficiency.

The authors report that adaptive distance measurement and gradient updates on decoupled manifolds prevent optimization from being dominated by semantic or structural variants and mitigate distribution-shift effects at test time.

narrative_sequence.summary: Test-time adaptation is used to adapt trained models to distributionally shifted test data, and recent graph methods operate with Euclidean-space augmentations and self-supervised objectives.
Graph data can combine semantic and topology-induced variations with different geometric patterns, making a single fixed geometry distort representations and mislead updates.
The paper introduces Riemannian geometry as a foundation for graph test-time adaptation and proposes GeoTTA to control update directions.
GeoTTA separates representations into hyperspherical and hyperbolic subspaces and performs prototype alignment with geometric consistency on matched-curvature manifolds.

The authors report that decoupled-manifold optimization mitigates distribution-shift effects and achieves superior source-free adaptation performance across ten public benchmarks with competitive efficiency.

source_observation.claim: Semantic and structural variations in graph data may follow different geometric patterns.

interpretation.claim: Representation and adaptation objectives may benefit from separating variation types rather than forcing them into one geometry.

application.claim: For graph adaptation tasks with heterogeneous variation, consider geometry-specific subspaces and geometry-matched consistency objectives.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that multiple geometries are necessary or beneficial for graph tasks without heterogeneous semantic and structural variation.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the ten benchmarks or their domains.
No quantitative results, baselines, ablations, or efficiency measurements are provided.
Details of the model architecture, optimization procedure, and curvature selection are omitted.
